_comment: §3.5 labeled corpus, built from REAL user prompts, not invented ones.
Source: .llamacli/state/prompt-history.json (50 entries, this machine, 2026-09~10).
That file was the only session-derived record of what the user actually typed; there is
no transcript of assistant replies or tool calls on this box, so every label below is a
judgment about the REQUEST, made without seeing the answer.
TEXTS ARE BYTE-EXACT from the source file. An earlier hand-transcribed version had
collapsed whitespace AND silently repaired the user's typos (깋 푸시 멎 -> 깃 푸시 머지,
llama.x\x7fcpp -> llama.cpp). That is the worst possible drift for this corpus: the
typos and the stray control byte are exactly what the model receives, so 'fixing' them
measures a different input than the one that occurs. `text` must always be regenerated
from the source by index, never retyped. Verified byte-exact by corpus_verify.
Labels are POLICY, not 'the answer I would give':
kind:  slash = a UI command, never a task
ack   = a menu pick / one-word acknowledgement / continuation with no task content
status= 'is X working / did it apply' — answerable by inspection, no reasoning
task  = a real request
deep:  for kind=task only. true = needs code reading, multi-step work, or judgement
false = a lookup or a single mechanical action
Class balance is deliberately NOT rebalanced: deep 19 / shallow 3 is the real shape of
this machine's usage, and that imbalance is itself the finding (see report §2.4).
